title: Beef Stroganoff
subtitle: Russian sautéed beef in soured cream sauce
excerpt: Tender strips of beef fillet sautéed fast in butter with onion and mushrooms, finished in a sauce of soured cream, mustard, and beef stock. A classic Russian dish brought to international fame, ready in under thirty minutes when the beef is sliced correctly.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef Stroganoff is named after the Stroganov family, wealthy Russian merchants and landowners. The dish appears in Russian cookbooks from the mid-nineteenth century, where it consisted of sautéed beef cubes in a sauce of mustard and soured cream, without mushrooms or onions. The version with mushrooms and onions emerged later and became the international standard through Russian emigré cooking after the 1917 revolution, then American adaptation in the 1950s. The key technique is the very high heat used to sear the beef strips: they must be cooked so quickly that they barely colour before the sauce is added, remaining pink in the middle. The soured cream is added off the heat to prevent curdling.

content.text: The beef must be cut into thin strips across the grain and cooked over the highest possible heat. Too slow and it stews; too thin and it toughens. Soured cream will split if boiled: add it off the heat or over the lowest possible flame, just enough to warm it through.

items.preparation: cut into strips 1 cm wide and 5 cm long, across the grain
full-fat soured cream or creme fraiche works equally well

content.text: Season the beef strips generously. Heat half the butter and oil in a wide frying pan over the highest heat. Sear the beef in a single layer for 1 minute each side until browned. Do this in two batches to avoid steaming. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining butter to the pan. Cook the onion over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened. Add the mushrooms and cook for a further 5 minutes until golden and any liquid has evaporated.

Add the beef stock and mustard. Stir to combine and cook for 2 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in the soured cream. Return the beef and any resting juices. Stir briefly off the heat; the residual warmth will warm the beef through. Season and serve immediately over egg noodles or rice, scattered with parsley.
